The test image shows corn plants with prominent white/silvery parallel striping along leaves, with some areas appearing bleached or shredded. Key features:
- White to pale parallel stripes alternating with green tissue
- Leaves appear somewhat erect and tattered
- No discrete lesions or pustules visible

Top candidates: **Downy_mildew** (white parallel stripes, shredded appearance), **Maize_streak_virus** (yellow/white streaks along veins), **Stewarts_wilt** (pale streaks along veins).

Let me view reference images for these candidates.
The Maize_streak_virus reference (bottom-right panel) shows leaves with white/silver streaking very similar to the test image. Let me check a couple more candidates to confirm.

Now I have enough evidence. Let me compare the key visual features:

**Test image features:**
- Corn at field stage (tasseling/vegetative)
- Broad white/silvery parallel stripes covering large portions of leaves
- Multiple plants affected throughout the field
- Stripes run lengthwise along the leaf

**Comparison:**
- **Maize_streak_virus**: Reference bottom-right panel shows very similar broad white/silver stripes running along leaf length, and the field view (bottom-left) matches the test image's field appearance closely — multiple plants showing white-streaked leaves
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: Shows white stripes but more mosaic/patchy pattern; top-left shows broad single white stripe
- **Downy_mildew**: Younger plants, white stripes that become shredded/brown; test image plants appear older
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**: Purple/reddish discoloration — no match

The test image most closely matches **Maize_streak_virus** — the prominent broad white/silver parallel striping on multiple plants at field stage, visible in both close-up and field views, aligns with the Maize streak virus reference images and the characteristic narrow-to-broad yellow-white streaks caused by this geminivirus.
